audit.title: Call an API with HTTP Query Parameters

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The intro cleanly states the task ("send a request to a Decentralized Oracle Network to call the...API...returns the asset price for ETH/USD"). Weak: the `Examine the code` section leads with `FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` as an empty heading with no content, and the key parameter answer (`url`/`params` object) is buried mid-section rather than opening it.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong hierarchy — 7 headings, 0 level skips, 0 sections over 600 words, 32 bullets. Weak: an empty subsection and 0 tables; the makeHttpRequest parameters would extract better as a small table.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Good — real costs (`0.249819373001796045 LINK`), transaction hashes, request IDs, `subscriptionId`, gas concepts. Weak: 0 numerals carry units in prose; the `gasLimit` value is described but not given.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 17 external links including GitHub source, Remix, ethers, CryptoCompare API docs, and internal API reference. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Weak — no crisp liftable definition of key terms (DON, `Functions.makeHttpRequest`, `args`); terms are used inline without a one-sentence canonical statement near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, 0 og/twitter tags, no declared programmingLanguage. This is the largest scored gap.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Good — 4 substantive blocks with language tags and network context (Sepolia); simulation output shown. Weak: 1 untagged fence (the `params` object), 2 placeholder comments, and truncated JSON (`...`).

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Moderate — covers setup→run→examine, but no "how do I fetch a different asset price" answer-first section (it's buried in `args`), no troubleshooting/FAQ, no error-string coverage.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming of Chainlink Functions, DON, NPM package. "The code is self-explanatory" appears twice and adds nothing.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-linked Chainlink Functions tutorial showing how to pass HTTP query parameters to the CryptoCompare price API through a DON. Its biggest strengths are dense authoritative linking (7 primary-source links, full runnable scripts) and tight structure with no oversized sections. Its biggest opportunities are missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no dates) and thin query/symptom coverage — there is no troubleshooting or error-string content, and one heading (`FunctionsConsumerExample.sol`) is empty. Honest verdict: solid best-practice tutorial content undermined by absent structured metadata and no symptom-phrased retrieval hooks.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD and canonical/date metadata
recommendations.issue: measured facts — "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)", "canonical: MISSING", "datePublished absent / dateModified absent"
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: JavaScript`, and a canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent parse-trust and E-E-A-T; this page currently exposes none.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/how-to section for changing the asset pair
recommendations.where: new H3 under `Examine the code` or after `Tutorial`
recommendations.issue: the reusable answer is buried in the `args` bullet: "You can adapt `args` to fetch another asset price."
recommendations.change: Add a section titled "How do I query a different asset price (e.g. BTC/EUR)?" opening with the one-line answer: change `args` to `["BTC","EUR"]`, mapped to `fsyms`/`tsyms`.
recommendations.why: devs query by task/symptom; a question-phrased heading wins retrieval the concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Fill or remove the empty `FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` heading
recommendations.issue: heading with zero body content below it.
recommendations.change: Add 1–2 sentences describing the consumer contract's role and its `sendRequest`/`fulfillRequest` functions, or delete the heading.
recommendations.why: empty sections create dead chunks and break the extractability of the surrounding unit.

recommendations.title: Convert makeHttpRequest parameters to a table with a lead sentence
recommendations.issue: the untagged fence `{ fsyms: fromSymbol, tsyms: toSymbol }` and prose bullets
recommendations.change: Open with "`Functions.makeHttpRequest` accepts `url`, `params`, `headers`, and `method`." then a small table of param → value; tag the object fence as `javascript`.
recommendations.why: tables and a canonical lead sentence give engines extractable reasons and defend against parametric substitution of the generic `fetch` idiom.

recommendations.title: Add expected `gasLimit` value and note default response timeout inline
recommendations.issue: "Maximum gas that Chainlink Functions can use" — no number given
recommendations.change: State the concrete value used in the example (e.g. `gasLimit: 300000`) and keep the "waits for five minutes" figure prominent.
recommendations.why: quantitative parameters are among the highest-lift additions for citation.

recommendations.title: Remove filler phrasing
recommendations.issue: "The code is self-explanatory and has comments" (repeated)
recommendations.change: Replace with a one-line statement of what each script does.
recommendations.why: removes low-information prose; engines reward concise, informative text.

antiPatterns: Empty section: `FunctionsConsumerExample.sol` heading with no body.
Repeated filler: "The code is self-explanatory and has comments" appears twice.
Truncated code: JSON response ends in `...`, and one code fence is untagged (measured: 1 untagged).
No stuffing, no marketing fluff, no ambiguous cross-references detected.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; ensure this tutorial is indexed there.
Site-wide absence of `TechArticle` JSON-LD and canonical tags is likely templated; fixing at the template level benefits all tutorials, not just this page.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>` on future runs — head metadata could not be verified here, so the metadata score reflects measured absence in served HTML only.
